raw_response:
I farm by starting from what worked for me before, then I make small changes if the price of inputs or the weather looks different. On my 5 mu, I cannot play risky games. Wheat and maize are both important, and if one season goes wrong, the whole year gets tight. I have used well water for years, so I will not wait for the sky if the soil is dry. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed because the stand is better and the ears are more even than old seed. I will put most of the phosphorus into the base fertilizer, keep nitrogen a bit on the safe side, and give water at the key stages. Around here, if wheat is short of fertilizer or water in spring, yield drops fast, so I would rather spend a bit more than lose grain. For maize, I will use hybrid seed. In our place, hybrid maize gives steadier yield, and many people around me use it. I will keep fertilizer a little strong because maize eats a lot, especially after wheat. I will do rotary tillage, because it fits my labor and the field can be prepared fast. For pests, I will not spray blindly, but I will not save money on one needed spray either. I will do what I have seen work in nearby fields: wheat usually needs two to three rounds across the season, maize about two. Since some family members work off-farm, I will keep the plan practical, not too fancy, and rely on inputs that give clear return.
